findings.title: Revoke the previous local recovery set when writing to user storage
findings.body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, this helper leaves any existing recovery credential in the Keycloak database untouched. Existing federated users can have such credentials because the required action previously always created them locally. Credential validation can still fall back to the local recovery-code provider, so those old codes remain usable after the user regenerates their recovery codes. Remove the previously stored recovery credential after a successful external replacement, and cover the transition from locally stored to externally stored codes.

findings.title: Disable exhausted credentials in the storage that owns them
findings.body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by a user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById. That removes a Keycloak-stored credential, not the external credential exposed by the provider. If the provider retains the exhausted credential and reports it as configured, abandoning the subsequent setup action leaves the next login trying to render an empty recovery set; RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() and fails. Use the user-storage disabling path for an exhausted external credential rather than attempting only a stored-credential deletion.

findings.title: Exercise consumption of externally stored recovery codes
findings.body: The new test provider accepts any matching code without consuming it, while getCredentials reconstructs a completely unused recovery set on every call. Consequently, the same code remains valid indefinitely, the requested code number never advances, and allCodesUsed can never become true. The new integration test stops after one successful login, so it does not verify that the changed federated lookup observes consumption or exhaustion. Maintain consumption state in the test provider and test replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.
